newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary BUX index ends steady after profit-takings.
newsitem.headline: Hungary BUX index ends steady after profit-takings.

text.p: Hungary's BUX index changed little on Wednesday, although half of the traded shares dropped on profit-takings, including chemicals maker TVK and oil and gas company MOL, traders said.

"At the current price levels the bourse (Budapest Stock Exchange) seems to have reached a balance," said Peter Lencs of MKB Securities. "Prices are likely to stagnate until news increase the appetite for buying.
The BUX index closed up 0.09 percent or 5.49 points at 5,978.86 points.
Half of the 38 stocks which traded on Wednesday dropped, what dealers attributed to the slack interest of foreign investors.
Traders said that profit-takings came as a correction of a bull-run earlier this week, which raised the BUX to a new intra-day trading high of 6,012.20 points on Tuesday.
Some traders said the Czech government's fight for stabilising the crown made some investors, who are looking at the region, cautious, while other traders pla9ed down the significance of this impact.
The BUX index was pulled down mainly by MOL's and TVK's losses, which were slight, but both of these heavy-weight stocks traded in high turnover.
MOL dropped 10 forints to finish at 3,380.
Traders said investors locked in profits following the domestic and international offerings of MOL earlier this month.
"Many investors still have shares which were bought at a discount of some 10 percent," Lencs said.

New York Broker's Attila Gazdik said news about gas price rises expected for later this year would push MOL up, but some investors did not see the stock rising for the short term and they may have replaced their MOL shares with other stocks.

TVK closed at 2,695 forints, down 30. Traders attributed taht to profit-takings following a sharp rise in the past few months, while some of them quoted market talks referring to that TVK's second half 1997 results may be weaker than in the first half.
Despite the price falls on the Hungarian bourse, the index changed little, mainly thanks to drug maker Richter, which closed at 15,280 forints, up 205, traders said.
"Back in December, Richter stood at 8,0008forints," Gazdik said. "But the company is good, its results are good and it has outstanding prospects... Everybody recommends it to buy."
Some traders said the Hungarian market needed some good news to rise again, while others believed the BUX may firm already this week.
